homily:
Imagine a mother standing in a place where the world seems to be ending. The sky has turned dark, the air is thick with the weight of unspeakable loss, and every instinct of a human heart screams for the pain to stop. This is Mary. She is not a distant, marble statue; she is a mother whose heart is being pierced, just as Simeon once foretold. She stands at the foot of the Cross, not because she is strong in the way the world defines strength, but because she is present in the way love defines it. Love does not abandon. Love stays. Love stands, even when the ground beneath it is shaking.

There is a profound, quiet truth in the Gospel today: 'Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother.' She doesn't speak. She doesn't argue with God. She simply stands. There is an ache in that standing that every person in this room knows. It is the ache of the empty place, the silence that follows a vibrant voice, the quiet moments when you are left alone with the memory of a smile. I know for you, Alan and Thao, for you, Ryan, and for all who loved Benjamin, that 'standing' has become your way of life. You stand in the memory of his brilliance, his curiosity, his gentle laughter, and you stand in the reality of his absence.

Let us look at this image of the Mother and the Son. It is the hinge of our faith. When Jesus looks down from the Cross, he does not look at the Roman soldiers or the shouting crowds. He looks at his Mother, and he looks at the disciple whom he loved. He gives them to each other. 'Woman, behold, your son.' 'Behold, your mother.' In the midst of the greatest suffering the world has ever known, Jesus is building a family. He is ensuring that no one is left to carry the weight alone. He is saying that we belong to one another, that our sorrows are shared, and that even in the darkest hour, we are held in a communion of love that death cannot break.

Benjamin was a boy who understood this communion. You remember how he was always the first to offer a 'Good morning, Dad.' He was a boy who lived in connection. He didn't just exist; he engaged. Whether he was coding a new game, dreaming of his 'Con Chim Airlines,' or simply sitting quietly with his brother Ryan, Benjamin was always weaving himself into the lives of those he loved. He was a part of the Body of Christ, as St. Paul tells us in the reading from Corinthians. 'The body is not a single part, but many.' Benjamin was a vital, beautiful part of that Body. His smile, his braces, the way he looked at the world with such wonder—these were not just his; they were gifts to all of you. They were the ways God chose to show you His own love.

I want to speak directly to the ache you carry. Sometimes, we look for answers in the logic of the world—in the math that Ben loved so much, in the systems and structures he was so brilliant at understanding. We want a formula that explains the 'why' of our suffering. But the Cross offers no mathematical formula; it offers a Presence. It tells us that God does not stand far off from our pain. He enters it. He hangs upon it. He feels the sword pierce through his own heart, just as it pierces through yours. You are not alone in your grief. You are standing right where Mary stood, and Jesus is looking at you with that same love, inviting you to be part of his family, to lean on one another, and to trust that the story does not end at the foot of the Cross.

Ryan, my dear brother, you know this better than anyone. You carry the memory of your big brother in your heart, in your laughter, and in the quiet moments of your day. You are the one who knows the rhythm of his life. Do not let the silence of the room make you forget the music of his spirit. Keep living, keep dreaming, keep being the wonderful person you are. Every step you take, every joy you find, is a testament to the love you two shared. Benjamin is not gone; he is simply living in the light of the Father, where there is no more shadow, only the fullness of life.

Alan and Thao, you have loved your son with a perfection that is rare and beautiful. You have given him the world, and you have taught him how to see it with eyes of wonder. That love is not lost. It is the very thing that connects you to him now. When you feel the weight of the day, when the 'sword' of sorrow feels particularly sharp, remember that you are held. You are held by the God who knows what it is to lose a Son. You are held by the Mother who knows what it is to watch a child go to God. You are held by the community of faith that surrounds you, the family and friends who, like the women at the cross, are standing with you.

There is a temptation to blame, to search for a reason, to wonder if something could have been different. Let that burden go. It is a heavy stone that was never meant for your shoulders. God does not demand an accounting of your love; He only asks that you continue to live in it. You missed nothing. You loved him perfectly, and that love is the bridge that spans the distance between here and heaven. You are free to grieve, you are free to remember, and you are free to hope.

What can you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but it is a holy thing. The next time you see a plane climbing into the sky, or you see a bird in flight, or you feel the warmth of the sun on your face, don't just see the world. See the 'body' that we are all a part of. Whisper Ben's name, not as a goodbye, but as a greeting. Tell him, 'I am still here, and I am still loving you.' And then, listen for the quiet answer of the Spirit in your heart. You are part of a love that is larger than death, a love that is currently holding Benjamin in the peace of the Banquet, and that is holding you right here, right now, in the palm of God's hand. You are not alone. You have a Mother who stands with you, and a Brother who waits for you. Keep standing in that love. Keep trusting in that light. And know that, in the end, all will be well.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the peace of the Mother of Sorrows be your strength today and always.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin Đại Dương Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ.
For all who are grieving, especially Alan, Thao, and Ryan, that they may find comfort in God's presence and the hope of eternal life.

readings.label: Sivulliq Reading
readings.text: Brothers and sisters: As a body is one though it has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, are one body, so also Christ. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one Body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free persons, and we were all given to drink of one Spirit. Now the body is not a single part, but many. Now you are Christ’s Body, and individually parts of it.

readings.label: Psalm
readings.text: R. We are his people: the sheep of his flock. Sing joyfully to the LORD, all you lands; serve the LORD with gladness; come before him with joyful song. R. We are his people: the sheep of his flock. Know that the LORD is God; he made us, his we are; his people, the flock he tends. R. We are his people: the sheep of his flock. Enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with praise; Give thanks to him; bless his name. R. We are his people: the sheep of his flock. For he is good, the LORD, whose kindness endures forever, and his faithfulness, to all generations. R. We are his people: the sheep of his flock.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple there whom he loved he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son.” Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother.” And from that hour the disciple took her into his home.

day: Memorial of Our Lady of Sorrows

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - need a miracle here. We miss you so much and we’re not sleeping much. Ryan wish you were here, especially this upcoming Saturday to play the new version of Project Flight with him.
